name: Mirko Forastiere
summary: Mirko started as a PhD researcher at the department of Environmental Biology in November 2022. Mirko received his BSc diploma in Chemistry in 2020 at the University of Padua (Italy). In his thesis he focused on the effects and the disposal of a common organophosphate pesticide. He received his Msc degree in Evolutionary Biology in 2022 at the same University, dedicating his master's thesis to assessing the role of Chondrichthyes in the Mediterranean Sea trophic network. Mirko's current project aims to assess the effects of pesticides on the insects populations, and consequently to show the impact on trophic relationships and also potentially on human activities.

name: Ming Fricke
summary: Marcus Ming Fricke is an Industrial PhD researcher at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) on "Regenerative Built Environment Design through Ecosystem Services Provision" in collaboration with Henning Larsen Architects and supported by the Innovation Fund Denmark. Marcus Ming Fricke worked with European city administrations and graduated with honours from the first Norman Foster Institute Programme on Sustainable Cities. He holds a Master of Science degree with distinction from the Technical University of Munich in ‘Resource Efficient & Sustainable Building’ and is lead author of ‘Ecosystem Services guiding Built Environment Design’ in the Springer Nature Sustainable Development Goals Series. He is an alumni of the Oskar von Miller Forum, an independent education initiative of the Bavarian construction industry, and former sustainability consultant at ARUP. In 2020, he co-founded the German Collaborative which represented the Living Building Challenge (LBC) that is recognized as the world’s most rigorous performance based green building standard. He was the German Ambassador and is one of the first Living Future Accredited professionals (LFA) in Germany. The project develops the quantified integration of the ecosystem services concept into the built environment design process, together with the presentation of applied case studies. The overall objective is to realize regeneration potentials within built environment developments by consciously designing and systematically providing ecosystem services.

name: Christina Galafton
summary: As a PhD candidate at the Industrial Ecology department of CML, Christina focuses on the quantification of the environmental impacts of plastic emissions on terrestrial ecosystems. Christina obtained a BBA (Business Administration) at Hogeschool van Arnhem en Nijmegen, an MA (Sustainable Development Cooperation) at TU Kaiserslautern, and an MSc (Applied Environmental Sciences) at TU Koblenz. Before becoming a researcher at Fraunhofer UMSICHT in Germany in 2022 where she is conducting most of her research as a PhD candidate, she worked at an international steel and technology company and a non-profit organization. She started as a PhD candidate at the department of Industrial Ecology in September 2024. Christina focuses on the quantification of the environmental impacts of plastic emissions on terrestrial ecosystems, including their fate (redistribution to other environmental compartments, fragmentation, and degradation), exposure of organisms to the emissions, and resulting effects. She aims to develop a methodology to integrate the assessment of plastic pollution impacts in Life Cycle Impact Assessment.

name: Joseph Gent
summary: Joseph started his PhD at the department of Environmental Biology at Leiden University in early 2024. His research focuses on understanding the temporal dynamics of the relationship between environmental heterogeneity and biodiversity. Joseph is researching the temporal dynamics of the relationship between environmental heterogeneity and biodiversity. A range of spatial scales will be considered from the European level to a case study focussing on the dune ecosystem of Meijendel. The aim of the project is to gain a deeper understanding of fundamental ecology while also drawing out useful implications for biodiversity policy. Joseph obtained his integrated master’s degree in Biological Sciences at Wadham College, University of Oxford, in 2022. Within the bachelor's course he specialised in ecology and evolutionary biology. His master's thesis focused on understanding the mechanisms through which mental health benefits are delivered by urban vegetation at a population level. This GIS focused analysis was then continued working as a research assistant at the Long Term Ecology Lab in Oxford where he investigated the role of volatile organic compounds emitted by plants on wellbeing. Joseph began his PhD at the department of Environmental Biology at Leiden University in early 2024.

name: Daniel Zumel Gete
summary: Daniel is interested in unravelling the mechanisms that drive the evolution of living organisms and shape their ecological niches and geographic distributions. In January 2024, he started working as a PhD researcher at the Department of Environmental Biology of CML, where he investigates evolutionary dynamics within hybrid zones between species of the genus Triturus, using genetic data obtained from environmental DNA (eDNA). Daniel received his bachelor diploma in Biology in 2018 from Complutense University of Madrid (Spain), specializing in environmental sciences. During this stage, he gained practical experience as a wild animal keeper at two zoos in Spain, and volunteered at animal rescue and release centers in both Peru and Costa Rica. He then completed a Master’s degree in Tropical Biodiversity and Conservation at Menéndez Pelayo International University (Madrid, Spain; 2018-2020), with internships in several Natural Reserves of Costa Rica. His Master's thesis, conducted in collaboration with Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador (PUCE), resulted in the discovery of a new monophyletic group of species within the Pristimantis genus and the description of four new frog species. This collaboration with PUCE continues, focusing on addressing biodiversity shortfalls within this genus. In 2021, Daniel joined the Royal Botanical Garden, part of the Spanish National Research Council, CSIC (Madrid, Spain) as a Predoctoral Researcher. There, his work shed light on stress response mechanisms in bryophytes, notably the increase in the endoreduplication level in mosses under drought conditions. His contributions from this stage also included the description of two new Grimmia species from California (USA). Further advancing his skills, in 2022, he received a specialization diploma in Bioinformatic Analyses from Pablo de Olavide University (Sevilla, Spain), where he developed advanced skills in programming and genomic analysis. In January 2024, he joined Leiden University's Department of Environmental Biology at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) as a PhD researcher. Daniel’s PhD project focuses on investigating hybrid zones between Triturus species through the lens of molecular ecology, utilizing genetic data obtained from environmental DNA (eDNA). The primary objective is to gain a deeper understanding of the evolutionary dynamics within Triturus hybrid zones across Europe, ultimately facilitating more effective conservation strategies for these species. For an overview of Daniel's publications, you can follow this link.

name: Haye Geukes
summary: Haye started as a PhD researcher in the C-Scape program in November 2021. Haye obtained his BSc degree in Natural and Social Sciences at the University of Amsterdam in 2019, majoring in the Biological Sciences track of Ecology & Evolution. For his BSc thesis, he worked as a diver and research intern at St. Eustatius National Parks (STENAPA) where he investigated coral reef restoration, centring on Elkhorn coral (Acropora palmata). Additionally, he completed a minor in Practical Philosophy and a minor in Theoretical Philosophy, respectively focussing on liberal political philosophy and philosophy in arts and culture. In 2021, Haye received his MSc degree in Industrial Ecology at Leiden University and Delft University of Technology. Here, he specialized in Environmentally Extended Input-Output Analysis (E-IOA), using it for attributing scope-3 emissions to align investment portfolios with the Paris Agreements goals and working as a Teaching Assistant for the E-IOA course. For his MSc thesis, he turned to political philosophy again to investigate normative uncertainties in the North Sea Consultation (Noordzeeoverleg), in which the energy transition on sea was planned to enact the Dutch Climate Agreement. This research led to a publication on the moral role of the ‘healthy sea’ metaphor in this political negotiation process. Haye is currently working as a PhD researcher at the C-Scape program. His research focuses on the evaluation of nature-based solutions in policymaking and management for coastal climate adaptation.

name: Iman Goudarzi
summary: PhD researcher focusing on life cycle assessment and data-driven environmental modelling to support net-zero transitions in complex port and maritime systems. I am a PhD candidate at Leiden University in the Industrial Ecology group (CML), with a background in environmental engineering from politecnico di milano. My research experience spans environmental modelling and data science, with a strong focus on applying machine learning and high-performance computing to complex environmental systems. Previously, I worked as an environmental data scientist at the University of Milano-Bicocca and as a guest researcher at the Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency (PBL), where I developed data-driven models for climate and energy system analysis to support environmental decision-making. My PhD research focuses on developing a comprehensive and prospective Life Cycle Assessment framework for port-call operations, aiming to support data-driven decision-making for port decarbonisation and net-zero strategies. The research assesses current and future port-call configurations, integrates prospective energy system scenarios, and explores marine environmental impacts, with the Netherlands as a key case study.

name: Marvin Groen
summary: Marvin Groen's passion lies in leveraging his knowledge of GIS applications, adeptness in data analysis and extensive field skills to contribute significantly to the field of nature conservation. Groen is part of the BioClock consortium and will be researching the effect of artificial light at night on various trophic levels in an ecosystem. Groen worked as an (urban)ecologist at the Natural History Museum of Rotterdam carrying out surveys on biodiversity, mostly bats, plants and insects. Additionally, his tasks were writing reports for both governmental and commercial clients. He supervised several students with their master’s and bachelor’s theses. And, he was the expert in GIS and statistics within the company. For five years, Groen has been assisting and teaching in the minor ‘Biodiversity’ as part of the Biology bachelor's programme. The minor includes courses on field ecology and sampling methodology as statistics and GIS. We have several field weeks wherein the students gather field data which they will later in the course analyse. The collected data is also used in the long-term research scheme called the PolderLab. Besides this, Groen set up a company together with Kevin Groen, his twin brother who also works for the CML. They arrange, produce and present all sorts of nature communication activities, such as excursions, blogs and nature documentaries. And they have written a book, named The Wild Wild East. For more information visit their Instagram page. Groen did the master's Forest and Nature Conservation at the University of Wageningen and the master's Evolution, Biodiversity and Conservation Biology at Leiden University.

name: Sebastiaan Grosscurt
summary: ᅟSebastiaan Grosscurt is a behavioural ecologist focusing on the impact of noise and light pollution on the lives of animals. He works as a PhD candidate in sensory multistress at the Institute of Environmental Sciencies. During his bachelor's degree at Leiden University College The Hague, Sebastiaan chose the major Earth, Energy and Sustainability. For his thesis research, he delved into the effect of recreation on the spatiotemporal pattern in animal observations. He continued with an MSc in Forest and Nature Management at Wageningen University & Research, specializing in animal ecology. He focused his thesis research on the African lion (Panthera leo) and its prey. In a mixed-use landscape, Sebastiaan investigated whether the densities of wild prey and livestock determined the spatial use of lions. As a graduate ecologist, Sebastiaan first worked as a full-time journalist for Trouw and Investico, among others. He now divides his time between ecological research, journalism and science communication. In his PhD research, Sebastiaan quantifies the cumulative effect of light and sound pollution. Animals are increasingly confronted with these sensory forms of pollution. Sebastiaan investigates how the behavior of animals changes due to the interplay of light and sound.

name: Alena Gsell
summary: Alena is an aquatic ecologist with a strong background in epidemiology and a particular interest in parasitic fungi and the health of freshwater ecosystems. Alena began her academic journey by studying English and German language and literature, followed by a transformative year as a volunteer researcher with the Kalahari Meerkat Project in South Africa. She then completed her undergraduate studies in Biology at the University of Basel before pursuing a Master's degree in Epidemiology and Infection Biology at the Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute. There, she focused on assessing accessibility of domestic dog populations to rabies vaccination in Tanzania. Alena earned her PhD at the NIOO-KNAW in 2013, studying the role of parasites in maintaining host genetic diversity. Following her PhD, she worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the IGB-Berlin, evaluating early warning signals for regime shifts in lakes within the BioDiversa+ project, LimnoTip. She later returned to NIOO-KNAW with an NWO VENI grant to explore the role of parasitic fungi in aquatic food webs. Alena also worked as a researcher at Wageningen Food Safety Research, focusing on natural toxins, particularly cyanotoxins. She is currently a guest researcher at NIOO-KNAW, with her up-to-date publication list available here. Since 2023, Alena has been an assistant professor at the Department of Environmental Biology, Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Leiden University. She teaches courses on biodiversity, aquatic ecology, and global change within the Biology programs, the MSc program Governance of Sustainability, and the CML Minor in Sustainable Development. Alena is dedicated to fostering a safe, inclusive, and supportive research environment that promotes productivity, creativity, and well-being for all. Alena’s primary research explores the role of fungal infections in aquatic ecosystems, investigating how these infections influence ecosystem functions and health, especially under the pressures of global change. Her second research focus is on the resilience of aquatic ecosystems and water quality, with a particular emphasis on urban blue infrastructure. In many urban water bodies, cyanobacterial blooms pose significant challenges; therefore, her third line of research seeks to understand the drivers of these blooms and their toxicity, while also developing potential mitigation strategies. Across all these research areas, Alena adopts a network perspective, emphasizing the importance of interactions and drivers within food webs. Her research methodologies include combinations of controlled experiments to understand mechanisms, field observations to explore the complex interplay of multiple drivers, long-term data analysis, and modeling.

name: Jeroen Guinee
summary: Dr. ir. Jeroen Guinée (M) has worked at the Institute of Envi­ron­mental Scie­nces (CML), Le­i­den Un­i­ve­rsi­ty since 1987, focusing on the research areas of life cycle assessment (LCA) and substance flow analysis (SFA). Prof. Jeroen Guinée (M) is a Professor of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) at Leiden University in The Netherlands. He obtained his MSc in Environmental Sciences at Wageningen University and successfully defended his PhD in LCA in 1995 at Leiden University. His doctoral research focused on the development of an environmental LCA method and contributed significantly to the first LCA Guide in 1992. In 2002, he served as the project leader and editor for a seminal publication in the field of LCA, the "Handbook on Life Cycle Assessment: Operational Guide to the ISO Standards" which stands as one of the most respected works in this domain. He has (co-)authored over 100 scientific papers and contributed to various books. He imparts his extensive knowledge by teaching a course on LCA to second-year master's students. Additionally, he dedicates his time to supervising master and PhD students as well as Postdocs. Throughout his academic career, he has actively participated in numerous large EU-funded research consortia. In recent years, his research has been devoted to ex-ante LCA and Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD), aimed at supporting the development of more sustainable and innovative products and technologies.

Quantitative uncertainty in LCI

name: Sterre ter Haar
summary: Sterre is a PhD researcher and lecturer at the Industrial Ecology department of the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML). Her work on quantifying the effect of climate change on nutrient security and public health is partially funded by the Frontiers Planet Prize. She previously conducted research here at CML (multi-criteria decision analysis in life cycle assessment; environmentally extended input-output analysis) as well as at Oxford University’s Oxford Martin School (rapid food transitions), University Centre of Svalbard (energy balance; mercury deposition), Technical University of Delft (modelling non-Newtonian fluids), and University of Dayton (nanofabrication of microbe-fueled microelectromechanical systems). A graduate of the TU Delft-Leiden University Industrial Ecology program, her MSc thesis ‘The Direct Effect of CO2 Rise on the Plant Ionome: Implications For Exacerbating Global Malnutrition’ won the 2025 Stans Award for best student thesis as well as the 2025 Rachel Carson Prize for best WO thesis. This work was expanded in the Horizon 2020 project EU 1.5 ° Lifestyles. Before this, Sterre received a BSc in Applied Earth Sciences from the Technical University of Delft (’17), and four ASc from Sinclair College (’13) in Mathematics, Engineering, Chemistry, and Biology. Sterre is currently the lecturer for the MSc course ‘Sustainability Analysis in Python’. Previously, she was the teaching assistant for Methods: Analysing Physical Processes, Renewable Energy Systems, System Earth, and Introduction to Petroleum Engineering, and tutored for the Sinclair College Mathematics and Chemistry department. Sterre’s research aims to quantify the effects of environmental change on food and nutrient security in the context of global trade and its public health implications for different consumer groups.

name: Helias Udo de Haes
summary: Prof. Helias A. Udo de Haes graduated in 1968 in biology at Leiden University. He performed his PhD research in the Max Planck Institut für Verhaltensphysiologie, in Seewiesen, Germany. After some years at the Technical University in Delft he joined the new department on Environmental Biology at Leiden University. In 1978 he founded CML as an interfacultary institute at the same university, of which he became the first director. In 1986 he was appointed as professor in environmental sciences. Since the beginning of the eighties research regarding the development of tools for environmental systems analysis came on the agenda of the institute, in particular Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Substance Flow Analysis (SFA). Personally he has been very active in the field of LCA, mainly at an international level. For many years he has been chairman of the LCA Steering Committee of SETAC-Europe. Since 1995 he has contributed to the standardization of LCA under ISO. He took the initiative for the establishment of the UNEP/SETAC Life Cycle Initiative for identifying best available practice in Life Cycle Assessment and Life Cycle Management, of which he has been the first director. In October 2006 he retired as scientific director. He is now active in the field of sustainability certification of natural resources. He is chairman of the Dutch Timber Procurement Assessment Committee and of the CEN Technical Committee 383 on biomass for energy applications.

name: Rosalie Hagenaars
summary: Rosalie started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in April 2022. Rosalie obtained her BSc degree in Environmental Studies at Utrecht University in 2018. The topic of her BSc thesis was on the transition to nature inclusive agriculture for meadow birds. After this, she did the MSc in Industrial Ecology at Leiden University and TU Delft. During this MSc, she specialized in LCA during a project commissioned by Waternet. She also worked as a Teaching Assistant for the EE-IOA course. For her MSc thesis, she investigated the carbon and material footprint of the Dutch consumption of pharmaceuticals. She used both input-output analysis and a literature review of LCA studies on individual pharmaceuticals in her thesis. The MSc thesis was part of an internship at RIVM in the Green Deal Duurzame Zorg project.

name: Emilia Hannula
summary: Dr. Emilia Hannula is a soil ecologist passionate about all soil creatures and especially soil fungi. Emilia is an expert in soil ecology with special love for soil fungi. Her research focuses on understanding how composition, traits and interactions between soil biota regulate ecosystem functions, how disturbances affect soil biota and subsequent functions, and ultimately how soil biodiversity and functions can be restored. She works on topics such as plant-soil feedbacks, the effects of soil diversity on plant and animal health, temporal and spatial stability of microbiomes, effects of climate and land-use change on soil fungi, foodwebs, and functions, and on ways to steer soil fungal communities for better functioning (soil) ecosystem. She is especially interested in trait-based analyses of fungi and soil multifunctionality in relation to sustainable future. Her expertise includes tracing carbon through system using stable isotopes, (molecular) microbiome analysis, and networks. She completed her PhD in 2012 in Microbial Ecology department of NIOO-KNAW and Institute of Biology Leiden. After the PhD she did a post-doc in large European project (‘EcoFinders’) investigating the effects of land-use on soil fungal communities using molecular fingerprinting methods and tracing the carbon to soil organisms (DNA-SIP). After that she worked while in another European project (‘SoilCare’) and analysed soil fungi across Europe and further worked in another project as a post-doc in NIOO-KNAW department of Terrestrial Ecology on plant-soil feedbacks and soil fungi affecting plant communities and plant growth. In 2019 she gained personal funding from Tor and Maj Nessling foundation to study the effects of soil disturbances on soil fungi and carbon cycling in soils. She is currently a guest researcher in NIOO-KNAW and you can read about her previous work here. Since 2021, she has worked in the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) at Leiden University first as assistant professor (2021-2024) and currently as an associate professor (since 2024). She currently leads a NWO-KIC consortium linking soil health to human gut health and in 2024 obtained a VIDI-grant. She co-leads the programme on future food systems and leads the soil ecology group within CML. She strives to lead a group that is a safe, healthy, productive, and inclusive environment for everyone.

name: Daan Heeling
summary: Daan is working as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Leiden University. Daan Heeling is a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Leiden University. He holds an MSc degree in Industrial Ecology from Leiden University and TU Delft. His master’s thesis focused on the impacts of alternative food production systems on the Dutch spatial layout. During his MSc, he also followed courses at the Faculty of Architecture, with a focus on landscape studies, design, and sustainability. Combined with a background in economics and politics, this allows Daan to approach food system transitions from a broad, interdisciplinary perspective, integrating environmental, technological, spatial, and socio-economic considerations. Since completing his MSc, Daan has worked with Gertjan Meeuws, Paul Behrens, José Mogollón, and Jan Willem Erisman on exploring the potential future role of vertical farming within sustainable food systems. This collaboration resulted in co-first authorship of the Frontiers in Plant Science article “Think Sink, Not Source”, with several follow-up publications currently under review or in preparation. Daan started his PhD at CML in February 2026. In collaboration with Joran Lammers, José Mogollón, Paul Behrens, and Jan Willem Erisman, his focus is on developing future spatial representations of novel plant protein production systems in the Netherlands, as part of the NWO-funded project REAP2SOW. His research is driven by a broad curiosity into how future food production systems can become more resilient to environmental and societal change, while also highlighting the opportunities, benefits, and positive potential of these emerging systems. In addition to his academic work, Daan volunteers at the Community Supported Agriculture foundation “Het Zoete Land” in Leiden (interview in local student newspaper), contributing to the production of locally grown food for a community of over 100 members. Daan’s research aims to develop future spatial representations of potential plant protein production systems, integrating environmental, technological, land-use, and socio-economic perspectives to support resilient and sustainable food system transitions.

name: Reinout Heijungs
summary: Reinout Heijungs graduated in 1987 in theoretical physics from Groningen University. For three years he was lecturer in physiology at the Medical Faculty of Leiden University. Research was directed towards chaotic analysis of noisy time series. He then moved to the Institute of Environmental Sciences at Leiden University. Research focused on the development of life cycle assessment, and related theories on the boundary of economics and the environment. In 1997 he received his PhD for the thesis entitled Economic Drama and the Environmental Stage, which has been reissued as A Theory of the Environment and Economic Systems, at Edward Elgar Publishing. After taking PhD, he spent a four-years research period at the Department of Spatial Economics of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Until 2013 he was lecturer and researcher in environmental science at CML, with an emphasis on foundational and methodological aspects of models for the interaction of economy and environment. His main interest is the development and application of mathematical, statistical, computational and philosophical methods in environmental systems analysis, including LCA, SFA, and E-IOA. Since 2013, he works with VU Amsterdam, School of Business and Economics, Department of Operations Analytics. He still has a small task at CML. Please check my profile or this link for more details.

name: Patrik Henriksson
summary: Research focus on interactions between humans and the ocean, with emphasis on foods. professional experience; 2024-present Assistant Professor betweenthe Institute of Environmental Sciences, Leiden University and Stockholm Resilience Centre (Stockholm University) 2019-2024 Researcher at Stockholm Resilience Centre (Stockholm University), the Beijer Institute of Ecological Economics, and WorldFish 2015-2019 Post-doc at Stockholm Resilience Centre (Stockholm University), the Beijer Institute of Ecological Economics, and WorldFish 2010-2015: PhD thesis: Evaluating European Imports of Asian Aquaculture Products using Statistically Supported Life Cycle Assessments, Leiden University. ISBN: 978-94-6203-952-0-

name: Glenn Aguilar Hernandez
summary: Glenn is a researcher from Costa Rica that has developed his career in the sustainability field. He holds a bachelor degree in Chemistry from the University of Costa Rica and a master of Sustainability from the University of Sydney, Australia. He has combined experience in research and development from academic and non-academic areas in topics such as renewable energy, natural resources, and sustainability analysis. He worked as Associated Research and Bioenergy Expert in the School of Biosystems Engineering at the University of Costa Rica, where he collaborated on bioenergy projects and the Climate Change Adaptation Program. Likewise, he has experience in the development of biofuels at an industrial scale in Energias Biodegradables de Costa Rica. During his master's studies, he specialized on techniques for sustainability analysis and developed his capstone project at the Centre for Integrated Sustainability Analysis at the University of Sydney, where he contributed to the application of Multi-Regional Input-Output model in biodiversity studies. Glenn developed his PhD at CML focusing on a macro-level assessment of material circularity. This research was part of the Circular European Economy Innovative Training Network funded by European Commission under Marie Curie Actions. His research outcomes contribute to a better understanding of the environmental implications of a circular economy on a macro scale. Currently, he is working on two projects as a Postdoc. First, he is developing an assessment of the COVID-19 impacts on global supply chains, which is a collaboration with the Circular Industries Hub, Leiden-Delf-Erasmus Centre for Sustainability. Second, he is providing support to the coordination of the Work Package 3 in SCRREEN 2 Project, where he focuses on market analysis, trade, and prices of critical raw materials for the European Union.

projects.title: UNravelling the socioeconomic and environmental Impacts of Circularity in Latin America (UNICA)

name: Rutger Hoekstra
summary: Rutger Hoekstra is full Professor of Sustainable and Inclusive Wellbeing (Hoogleraar Brede Welvaart). He is an expert in post-growth researcher which aims to overcome societies’ focus on economic growth and profits towards Wellbeing, Inclusion and Sustainability. He leads the WISE Horizons project and is Work Package lead of the MERGE project, which both work on metrics, models, policies and narrative for sustainable and inclusive wellbeing. He was the co-chair of the UNECE/OECD/Eurostat Task Force which developed the Conference of European Statisticians Recommendations on Measuring Sustainable Development. In 2019, he published his book Replacing GDP by 2030.with Cambridge University Press. In the past, he has worked for/with the United Nations, World Bank, European Commission, OECD, European Central Bank, IMF, KPMG, Statistics Netherlands, Greenpeace, Global Reporting Initiative, Wellbeing Economy Alliance, ZOE Institute and many other organizations. Rutger Hoekstra has worked on well-being, inclusion and sustainability from an academic, governmental and business perspective. He has written two books (including) and has published numerous scientific publications on post-growth, sustainable development, globalisation, circular economy and big data applications. He was also Scientific Director of the True Value methodology at KPMG Sustainability. He currently leads the WISE Horizons project which works on metrics, models, policies and narrative for sustainable and inclusive wellbeing (brede welvaart in Dutch). Rutger’s research interest include post-growth/beyond-growth, Beyond-GDP, wellbeing/sustainability policy, inequality, environmental economics using input-output techniques, environmental accounting, structural decomposition analysis, globalisation, circular economy.

name: Lingli Hou
summary: Lingli started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in September 2022, conducting research on the built environment and sustainability. Lingli Hou is PhD Candidate of Industrial Ecology at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) at Leiden University. Lingli obtained her Master of Environmental Economics from Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences in 2022, and bachelor of Economics from Nanjing University in 2018. During her master study, Lingli focused on the relationship of economy, urbanization and the environment. Specifically, she applied spatial models and geographic information systems (GIS) to explore the effect of economic growth and urbanization on air pollution, trying to figure out methods to improve air quality from the perspective of Environmental Economics. Lingli’s research interests include the built environment and sustainability. She is currently conducting research on material stocks/flows of construction materials of Belt & Road Initiative projects and improving material efficiency.

name: Jie Hu
summary: Jie Hu started as a PhD researcher at the Environmental Biology department of CML in September 2022. Jie received her master's degree in Zoology at Lanzhou University in 2022. At Lanzhou university, Jie focused on the parental consumption of nestlings’ feces in grey-backed shrikes, and she found probiotics and beneficial metabolites in the feces of nestlings may influence the parental consumption behaviour. Jie started as a PhD candidate at the Environmental Biology department of CML in September 2022. Jie’s research focuses on how the diversity of the birds responds to the environmental heterogeneity cross scales.

name: Mingming Hu
summary: Mingming Hu applies industrial ecology methods to support the sustainable transition of the built environment. She obtained her PhD in May 2010 with the dissertation Dynamic Material Flow Analysis to Support Sustainable Built Environment Development. Her doctoral research revealed the long-term oscillation pattern of China’s construction sector, projecting a sharp decline in housing demand from around 2020 to 2050 and a sustained increase in demolition waste throughout the 21st century. These projections have proven remarkably prescient, as China has entered the “post-overbuilding era” she identified more than a decade ago. Mingming Hu is an Associate Professor in Industrial Ecology whose research applies quantitative sustainability assessment to support the transition towards carbon-neutral, circular, and climate-resilient built environment. Drawing on an interdisciplinary background in building engineering, construction management, and environmental science, she develops scientific insights and practical tools to advance sustainable urban development. Mingming obtained her PhD in Environmental Science from Leiden University in 2010 with the dissertation Dynamic Material Flow Analysis to Support Sustainable Built Environment Development: Case Studies on Chinese Housing Stock Dynamics. Prior to this, she earned an MSc in Mechanical Engineering from Chongqing Jianzhu University (China), where she specialized in ground-source heat pump systems. Before joining CML in 2006, she worked for five years at the Chongqing Construction Commission, overseeing environmental infrastructure projects. Her research integrates dynamic Material Flow Analysis (dMFA), Life Cycle Sustainability Analysis (LSCA), and spatial analysis to understand how buildings, infrastructure, materials, and urban systems evolve over time. In her doctoral research, she projected the long-term dynamics of China’s construction sector, forecasting declining housing demand and increasing demolition waste decades before these trends became evident. Mingming’s current research focuses on three interconnected themes: built environment metabolism, circular construction supply chains, and spatial opportunities for urban sustainability. Her work addresses topics such as building stock dynamics, circular construction hubs, urban green infrastructure, and resilient cities, with the aim of accelerating the transition towards resource-efficient, resilient and biodiverse urban systems. She has played a leading role in numerous European and international research projects and has contributed significantly to two decades of collaboration between CML and Chinese research partners. She currently leads projects including ReSURE2 on urban resilience, CirCol on circular collaboration in the built environment, and RAW, an EU Pathfinder project on the bio-based and circular transition of the architecture, engineering, and construction sector. Previously, she initiated and coordinated several major Sino-Dutch projects including SIP project on industrial symbiosis and energy efficiency, and the Multigreen project, which supports greener, climate-resilient cities in both countries (See video). The partnership continues through the FOREWARD project, where the Netherlands and China work jointly to improve their water systems. She also initiated a series of European Horizon projects, including ICEBERG, HISER and VEEP, on construction and demolition waste recycling, and the EU FP7 C2CA project on concrete recycling, the Asia-Link ProtEA project on dynamic material flow analysis, the Dutch InnoMan project on waste management methodologies. In addition to her work at Leiden University, Mingming supervises graduate students at Chongqing University, where she holds a visiting scientist position.

name: Pablo Ilgemann
summary: Pablo started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in July 2023 and is working on the Circular Circuits project from the NWO. Pablo received his Bachelor diploma in Political Science: International Relations and Organizations in 2020 from Leiden University. In 2023 he graduated from the joint master program of Industrial Ecology at Leiden University and TU Delft. During this time Pablo spent 1 year at NTNU in Trondheim, where he completed his master thesis. In his thesis he developed a Python model to estimate the concrete volume of residential building foundations in Trondheim. After working briefly on LCAs in the sustainability consulting and finance sector, Pablo began his PhD at the Institute of Environmental Science at Leiden University in July 2023. Pablo works on the Circular Circuits project from the NWO. This multidisciplinary research project is focused on exploring the potential of circularity in the electronics sector. The research will try to solve challenges in modelling and assessing, such as high product complexity, new technological developments and growing consumer markets. Personally, he is very interested in the use of Python for scenario modelling and to solve complex issues. Feel free to send an email if you have any questions or want to collaborate.

projects.title: Circular Circuits

name: Robert Istrate
summary: Robert is an environmental engineer whose research lies at the intersection of sustainable resource management and decarbonization, assessing the environmental and economic benefits and trade-offs of natural resource use and waste valorization in industrial decarbonization. His work is grounded in the life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology and integrates other approaches such as scenario analysis, mathematical optimization, techno-economic analysis (TEA), and material flow analysis (MFA). Robert Istrate is Assistant Professor of Industrial Ecology at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) of Leiden University. Prior to joining CML, he held a postdoctoral researcher position in the Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences at ETH Zurich (2022-2023), where he conducted research on decarbonization pathways for the chemical industry. Robert earned his PhD in Industrial Technologies from Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (Spain, 2022), focusing on the assessment and optimization of waste-to-energy strategies within the context of the circular economy. He obtained his MSc in Energy and Fuels from Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (Spain, 2018) and his BSc in Environmental Engineering from Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (Spain, 2017). Robert's current research interests include: He primarily develops these research lines within several European research projects. He coordinates work packages on the assessment of environmental impacts of raw materials supply scenarios in the RAWCLIC and HiQ-LCA projects. He also contributes to the MaDiTraCe project, exploring the integration of life cycle assessment in certification schemes for critical raw materials, and the TranSensus LCA project, where he works on harmonizing the life cycle assessment methodology for zero-emissions vehicles Beyond his research, Robert coordinates the Sustainability Area Study - The Netherlands course in the Sustainable Development Minor and the Life Cycle Assessment course offered by Leiden University College.

projects.title: Circular Circuits

name: Shruti Jain
summary: Shruti's research focuses on the resilience and environmental impacts of global food systems. Shruti is a PhD candidate in Geography and the Environment at the University of Oxford, where her research involves mapping food flow networks at subnational scales using predictive modelling, projecting future food flow networks under socio-economic pathways and dietary change scenarios, and estimating the environmental impacts of food supply chains. Previously, she has consulted with the World Bank’s LSMS team on the 50x2030 Initiative, led agricultural data science at Atlas AI, and worked at UC Berkeley’s Global Policy Lab. Shruti's current research aims to integrate food system models with microdata on consumer diets and production practices to better attribute socio-economic and environmental impacts of food systems to individual consumer and producer groups.

name: Annegeke Jansen
summary: Annegeke started as a PhD researcher at CML in February 2023. Annegeke started her studies with an International Bachelor of Economics and Business Economics in 2012 at the Erasmus University of Rotterdam. Later on, in 2014, she did a bachelor in Philosophy while continuing her studies in economics. In 2017 she started her Master in International Economics. She analysed systemic risk of the European financial system for her thesis. After her studies, Annegeke worked at the Ministry of Finance in The Hague. During the first two years, she did a traineeship and worked within four different divisions. She worked on a variety of topics related to financial markets, foreign financial affairs, government bonds and state-owned enterprises. After her Traineeship in 2020, Annegeke got a position at the division for State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs). She worked on the state-ownership in FMO and Gasunie and the development of a policy regarding responsible business conduct/ESG for all SOEs. In addition, she was secretary to a sustainability group within the Ministry with the goal to stimulate coordination and knowledge-sharing between different divisions. Annegeke participates in the 'WISE Horizons' project with the goal to embed Beyond-GDP thinking into the European and Global Policy agenda. She will work on the development of indicators of Wellbeing, Inclusion, Sustainability and the Economy (WISE) and investigate determinants and historical developments related to wellbeing.

name: Andrea Herrera Jaramillo
summary: Andrea started her PhD at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) in March 2022 and resumed active research in June 2025 after a period of leave. Andrea has eleven years of experience at the intersection of design and circular economy, spanning consultancy, applied research, and academia across Latin America and the Caribbean. She has worked with the Organization of American States (OAS), the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (CEPAL/ECLAC), Universidad de Bogotá Jorge Tadeo Lozano and the Colombian consultancy firm CAIA Ingeniería S.A. She holds a BSc in Product Design Engineering from Universidad EAFIT (Colombia), and a MSc in Industrial Design Engineering from University of Twente, with a thesis on Cradle-to-Cradle decision support model for building design. As a PhD candidate at the CML, Andrea is focusing on applying Industrial Ecology and Circular Design to support circular economy decision-making in Colombia's key economic sectors. Her first paper presents a co-created Circular Design Model developed with companies in Colombia and Peru. Her current research applies Material Stock and Material Flow Analysis to cultural heritage buildings in Bogotá, in collaboration with the Instituto Distrital de Patrimonio Cultural de Bogotá (IDPC).

name: Xinpeng Jin
summary: Xinpeng became a PhD candidate at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in October 2022, whose research interest lies primarily on land and food system sustainability. Xinpeng received his MSc degree in Center for Agricultural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CARR, CAS). During his master period, Xinpeng focused on the nitrogen management of crop-livestock system, especially from the perspective of spatial optimization. Combining material flow analysis and multi-indicator evaluation (based on DPSIR and SDGs frameworks), Xinpeng and his colleagues depicted a sustainable livestock production pattern in China. Xinpeng’s preliminary research topic is to find pathways to achieve a sustainable food system in China.

name: Tycho Jongenelen
summary: Tycho started as a PhD researcher at Leiden University for the Nationaal Kennisprogramma Stikstof in collaboration with the Meteorology and Air Quality group of Wageningen University and Research, RIVM, TNO and KNMI. Tycho received his bachelor’s degree in environmental sciences at Wageningen University and Research in 2019. Here, he specialized in environmental policy, geo-information sciences and advanced statistics. For his bachelor’s thesis, he analysed the transition from flying to travelling by train from a social scientific perspective. In 2022, Tycho received his master's degree in industrial ecology at Leiden University and TU Delft, where he learned to approach wicked problems from a systems thinking perspective. During his master, he further specialised in biogeochemical cycles, atmospheric modelling and climate change at Wageningen University and Research. For his thesis, he researched the capabilities of machine learning to model surface ammonia concentrations in the Netherlands by using ground and satellite data. This thesis was in collaboration with the Climate, Air and Sustainability group of TNO. Tycho participates in the Nationaal Kennisprogramma Stikstof and is researching the atmosphere–biosphere measurements and models of reactive nitrogen to improve the current nitrogen deposition models in the Netherlands.

name: Kaushar Kagzi
summary: Kaushar started as a PhD researcher/Junior Lecturer at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) in January 2023. Kaushar received her Honours Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Toronto in 2018, where she double majored in Conservation and Biodiversity & Human Biology. In 2021, Kaushar obtained her M.Sc. in Biology from McGill University. Her thesis comparatively investigated the utility and applicability of environmental DNA (eDNA) and environmental RNA (eRNA) in characterizing zooplankton biodiversity in freshwater ecosystems. Following the completion of her M.Sc., in 2022 Kaushar worked as a Research Assistant at McGill University where she comparatively assessed the persistence and degradation dynamics of eDNA and eRNA based on genomic origin using metabarcoding methods.

name: Harsha Ramesh Kandackappalli
summary: Harsha is a PhD candidate who starts at CML in September 2026, working to map the stocks and flows of chemicals used throughout textile production. Harsha previously served as Program Lead for the End Textile Waste Alliance at Green Worms Pvt. Ltd, where she led partnerships and supported post-consumer textile waste management operations. Before that, she held the role of European Business Development and Partnerships Consultant at Green Worms, focusing on business development strategies. Before her journey with Green Worms, she was Production Lead at Ragnarök Clothing in Zwolle, leading the supply chain team. She also worked as a Practitioner at the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (AMFI), managing various laboratory operations. Harsha holds a Bachelor of Design and AAS degree in Textiles from NIFT Delhi and FIT New York, an MSc. in Innovative Textile Development from Saxion University of Applied Sciences, and a Master's in Business Management from Maastricht University (MSM). Chemicals are essential to nearly every stage of textile production, fibre preparation, yarn spinning, fabric formation, garment confection, and finishing & yet their flows and potential points of accumulation are rarely captured in material flow analysis (MFA) or life cycle assessment (LCA) of textiles. Harsha's PhD aims to address this gap by developing an open-source database of chemicals used at major textile production stages, contributing to ongoing efforts such as the PlastChem database and the Départ de Sentier taxonomy. Using industrial ecology tools, the project assesses chemical stocks and flows, maps data availability to support LCAs, product environmental footprints (PEF), and digital product passports (DPP), and collaborates with stakeholders across industrial ecology, toxicology, and policy to inform safe and sustainable by design (SSbD) initiatives across the textile value chain.

name: Hazal Kandemir
summary: Dr. Hazal Kandemir is a fungal taxonomist who is interested in the molecular investigation of the evolutionary traits within fungi. She also contributes to the field by describing novel fungi and actively participating in the improvement of fungal nomenclature. Hazal completed her PhD in 2022 in the Center of Expertise in Mycology of Radboud University Medical Center/CWZ Hospital, focusing on the ecology, phylogeny, and taxonomy of medically important fungi that are capable of degrading keratin. After her PhD, she did a post-doc at the Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) in a large national project called ARISE. In this project, she worked on building a database and molecular identification tools for Dutch soil fungi. She was also actively involved in an international Mycobiomics project that explores the mycological biodiversity for beneficial secondary metabolites and potential biocontrol agents, as well as the ecology and taxonomy of fungi. As a part of this project, she identified novel soil fungi and investigated the fungal diversity in different soil ecosystems in South Africa. Besides her research, Hazal enjoys organizing scientific events. She served as convener of the International Society for Human and Animal Mycology (ISHAM) Onygenales Working Group to bring scientists working on the same research topic together. Additionally, she served as a representative on the KNAW PhD and Postdocs Board to organize seminars, workshops, and social events for the PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers. Since October 2024, she works as a postdoctoral researcher to identify and measure relevant traits in soil fungi for important soil functions, in the Department of Environmental Biology, Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML).

name: Martijne Kannekens
summary: Martijne has started her PhD research on sustainable rice cultivation on peatlands in Northwest Europe in September 2025, focusing on greenhouse gas emissions, biodiversity impacts, integrated crop-livestock systems, and socio-economic transition pathways. BSc Biology at Leiden University (with a minor at University of British Colombia Vancouver and a minor at Erasmus University College Rotterdam), and MSc Industrial ecology at Leiden University and Technical University Delft Exploring rice cultivation as a sustainable future for agriculture on peatland in Northwest Europe

name: Raili Kary
summary: Raili's research applies MFA to EAF slag flows in the DiversEAFy project, enabling circular slag valorisation for low-carbon steelmaking. Raili has an undergraduate degree in Materials Science and Engineering at the University of Toronto, Masters Degree in Mechanical Engineering at Memorial University of Newfoundland. Furthermore, she has professional experience from Algoma Steel Inc. within the Environmental Control and Strategy departments. Raili works on the DiversEAFy project, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment. Within the EU Horizon project DiversEAFy, she uses material flow analysis to map and quantify slag flows across the EAF steelmaking value chain — supporting the valorisation of steelmaking slags.

name: Lena Kilian
summary: Lena Kilian is an assistant professor at the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML). Her work focuses on using environmentally-extended input-output analysis to estimate and analyse consumption-based emissions. Before joining Leiden University, Lena worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Leeds and the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. Prior to this, Lena completed her PhD at the University of Leeds in Data Analytics and Society, with a focus on consumption-based emissions of UK households. In addition to this she has an MSc from King’s College London in Sustainable Cities and a BSc from the University of Glasgow in Psychology with Sociology. Lena is particularly interested in subnational distributions of emissions to assess carbon inequalities as well as spatial differences in footprints. Moreover, from 2022-2025 she contributed to the construction of the UK’s Multi-Regional Input-Output (UKMRIO) model.

name: Rene Kleijn
summary: René Kleijn holds an MSc in chemistry and a PhD in Industrial Ecology both from Leiden University. He is now an associate professor at Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) at Leiden University. René Kleijn serves as a Professor of Resilient Resource Supply at Leiden University in the Netherlands, building on his background in Chemistry (MSc) and Industrial Ecology (PhD). He currently heads the Department of Industrial Ecology at the Institute of Environmental Sciences, working alongside 25 senior staff members, 12 postdocs, and about 70 PhD students. René has contributed to the development of Industrial Ecology and participated as a founding member of the International Society of Industrial Ecology. His work includes involvement in more than 15 EU-funded research projects and contributions to the "Groeien met Groen Staal" Growth Fund project, which focuses on sustainability in the Dutch steel sector. He helped establish the Leiden-Delft master's program in Industrial Ecology, which has grown into one of the largest educational programs in the field. His research applies quantitative methods such as Substance and Material Flow Analysis and Life Cycle Assessment across various industries including chemical, energy, mining, and recycling. Through this work, he aims to provide evidence-based insights to industry and policy stakeholders. Current research interests include critical raw materials, supply chain resilience, responsible sourcing, circular economy approaches, and understanding the material requirements of the energy transition
