name: Shijie Wei
summary: Shijie started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in October 2020. Shijie received his master and bachelor degrees of Mining Engineering from China University of Mining & Technology (Beijing) and Inner Mongolia University of Science & Technology in 2020 and 2017 respectively. In his master research, the economic advantages and CO2 emissions reduction potential of China’s coal-fired power plants with carbon capture and storage were systematically evaluated. He also participated in the projects of China-Africa Renewable Energy Technology Transfer supported by United Nations Development Programme and National Assessment Report on Oceans and Climate Change (2016-2020) initiated by State Oceanic Administration, People’s Republic of China. From October 2020, he entered CML to conduct PhD study. Optimizing the global use of biomass resources to combat climate change: meeting societal needs while maximizing the potential of ecosystems to provide biomass and sequester carbon.

name: Hidde Weistra
summary: Hidde will work for four months as a Research Assistant at CML to publish his MSc Thesis. Hidde researches assessment methods for supply chain vulnerability for Critical Raw Material dependent technologies.

name: Niels van der Windt
summary: Niels is a PhD researcher working with Naturalis, Wageningen University, and the Environmental Biology department of CML. He studies the symbiosis between sponges, their microbes, and their potential for natural product discovery as part of the European MARBLES project. Niels received both his BSc degree 'Biology' in 2016 and MSc degree 'Biodiversity and Sustainability' in 2020 at Leiden University. During his BSc internship he worked on sponge taxonomy and ecology by studying the predator-prey relationship between sponges and nudibranchs. Niels got fascinated by sponges because of their simplistic body plan, but very complex interactions with the environment and their importance for ecosystem functioning. During his master Niels continued working on sponges, where he started using molecular techniques to elucidate the relationship between coral boring sponges and a specific group of symbionts called Symbiodiniaceae. Overall Niels gained a great deal of experience working in the molecular lab by his internships, and by working as a technician at the molecular laboratories of Naturalis Biodiversity Center. Now Niels aims to identify the most promising ecosystems for Natural product discovery in Sponges. Using an integrative multi-omics approach Niels links global sponge biodiversity patterns to both overall microbial diversity and biosynthetic gene cluster (BGCs) diversity in sponges in a variety of marine environments, such as the deep sea, coral reefs and mangroves.

name: Che Xiao
summary: Che is a PhD candidate in Industrial Ecology at Leiden University, focusing on safe, sustainable, and circular design and decision support in the energy and healthcare sectors. Che Xiao is a PhD candidate at the Department of Industrial Ecology, Leiden University. He is part of the Horizon Europe project ENKORE, where he works on developing new ways to make the healthcare sector safer, more sustainable, and more circular. His academic journey began in electrical engineering at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, where he designed a low-carbon operational mechanism for an industrial park. This project, which received top marks, first sparked his interest in sustainability and large-scale system design. Before starting his PhD, Che completed a cum laude MSc in Industrial Ecology at Delft University of Technology and Leiden University (joint degree). His thesis examined the interaction between renewable energy technologies and circular economy strategies, combining prospective life cycle assessment (pLCA) and dynamic material flow analysis (dMFA). This work deepened his interest in methodological innovation to connect decarbonisation with circularity. Che is an interdisciplinary and methodologically oriented researcher who enjoys working at the crossroads of engineering, sustainability science, and policymaking. He has a strong background in electrical engineering as well as expertise in prospective LCA and dynamic MFA. His current research explores how Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design (SSbD) principles can be integrated into real-world product innovation and aligned with evolving regulations such as the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR). He seeks to create practical design and decision-support tools that help researchers, companies, and policymakers navigate trade-offs and generatively chart pathways toward a climate-neutral and resource-efficient future. Beyond his academic work, Che values philosophy as a way of deepening perspectives on science and society. He finds inspiration in Chinese Neo-Confucianism and German classical philosophy, both of which guide his search for balance between knowledge, ethics, and the flourishing of life.

projects.title: ENKORE: Designing a sustainable future for the European Healthcare Sector

name: Brenda Miranda Xicotencatl
summary: Brenda is a PhD candidate researching the sustainability of future recycling pathways to produce rare-earth magnets. Brenda is a PhD candidate at the Industrial Ecology department of the Institute of Environmental Sciences of Leiden University (CML). She holds a BSc in Chemical Engineering and an MSc in Industrial Ecology. She has experience working in the Chemical Industry and collaborating with technology developers in the environmental and economic assessment of novel technologies towards a sustainable transition. For example, she has contributed to the Horizon 2020 projects HISER and SUSMAGPRO. As part of the SUSMAGPRO project, funded by the European Commission, her current research explores the sustainability of recycling pathways to produce rare-earth magnets. She is currently assessing the impact of possible future technological developments on the industrial implementation of a recycling supply chain for neodymium magnets in Europe, in contrast to their supply from mines.

name: Tales Yamamoto
summary: Tales started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in February 2019. Tales graduated at the University of Graz in 2018, where he obtained his MSc degree in Sustainable Development. He also received a BEng degree in Chemical Engineering from the University of Campinas in 2010. Prior to CML, Tales worked for two years in the mining industry in different locations in Brazil, including the Amazon region. During this period, his tasks involved developing water balance for a beneficiation plant, overseeing the operation of the tailings systems and its safety, and reporting to regulatory bodies. Tales also worked as a consultant in the sugar and alcohol sector, developing industrial improvements and conducting feasibility studies. Tales participates in the EIT RawMaterials PANORAMA project that aims to produce an information service containing data of global flows and stocks of different materials and products. This will enable more informed decision making for various stakeholders to improve materials management and implement more sustainable practices.

name: Han Yu
summary: Han began her PhD in Industrial Ecology in November 2023, focusing on performance-oriented urban planning. Her research aims to bridge the gap between energy-efficient urban development and the design process. Han Yu received her Master's degree in Architecture from the College of Architecture and Urban Planning at Tongji University in 2023. Beyond architecture design, she has a strong interest in performance simulations at broader levels. Her research also focuses on optimization through data analysis and parametric modeling, aiming to transform urban spaces into highly energy-efficient, sustainable environments in response to climate change challenges. She joined the Institute of Environmental Science (CML) at Leiden University in November 2023 to pursue her doctoral degree. Han's doctoral project starts from investigating the relationships between urban morphology and residential energy consumption, towards to achieve positive-energy goals and enhance microclimate comfort in built environments across different scales. Her research topic, ‘The Impact of Urban Morphology Indicators on Building Energy Consumption: The Relationship, Mechanism and Redevelopment’. After exploring the intricate relationship via available data and revealing the underlying mechanisms, the potential impacts combined with materials and transportation on carbon emissions from an urban morphology perspective will come afterwards.

name: Zihao Yuan
summary: Zihao started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in October 2021. Zihao got his bachelor diploma in 2017 at School of Astronautics where for his graduation design he devised part of the thermal management of a satellite. From 2019 to 2020, he participated in a project in collaboration with Daqing Oilfield in China and the data assimilation strategy and software for Petroleum History Matching was developed by the research team. Then in 2021, he received his MSc diploma. Zihao does his research at SRON (Netherland Institute of Space Research) to find methods for improving the performance of satellite aerosol property retrieval by using neural networks and deep learning.

name: Jiaxin Zhang
summary: Jiaxin started as a PhD researcher at the Environmental Biology department of CML in September 2022. Jiaxin received her undergraduate degree in Environmental Ecological Engineering at East China Normal University in 2019 where for her final thesis she compared six indexes describing species roles, simulating extinction cascade effects by using Topological Coextinction Model and Stochastic Coextinction Model in 45 pollination networks, to find the best index reflecting the impact of extinction cascade on the functional niche of species in pollination networks. Later in 2022, Jiaxin received her master degree in Ecology at East China Normal University. During that period, Jiaxin supplemented her work about her bachelor thesis. She used one new method and one common method to identify the best index in pollination networks. Additionally, she applied the index to identify keystone species in East Asia. Jiaxin started as a PhD candidate at the Environmental Biology department of CML in September 2022. Jiaxin’s research is focus on pollination networks by environmental DNA (eDNA).

name: Jianhong Zhou
summary: Jianhong’s research topic is on plasticity and adaptation rates of plant species to changing climatic conditions, which focuses on the application of a trait-based approach to analyze the global pattern of intraspecific variability using plasticity and genetic adaptation trait databases Jianhong Zhou received her MSc (2015) degree in Ecology from East China Normal University (ECNU), Shanghai, China. She conducted her master research in an enclosed tidal wetland located at the east of Chongming Island to investigate the soil salinity dynamics after reclamation and its effect on plant growth in the context of climate change by long-term monitoring. During her master study, she was awarded a fund from ECNU as a visiting student to the University of California, Riverside, USA for three months. In 2016, she received CSC scholarship to study in the Netherlands for a doctorate. She spent one year at Soil Physics and Land Management Group in Wageningen University. Since September 2017, she has joined the Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) under the supervision of Professor Peter van Bodegom to pursue her doctorate degree. Jianhong’s research topic is on plasticity and adaptation rates of plant species to changing climatic conditions, which focuses on the application of a trait-based approach to analyze the global pattern of intraspecific variability using plasticity and genetic adaptation trait databases. The aim of her research is trying to find out the mechanisms underlying plant plasticity and the different responses of plant species to climate change, which will help to predict species assembly within communities under future climate conditions.

name: Jinhui Zhou
summary: Jinhui started as a PhD researcher at the Industrial Ecology Department of CML in September 2019. Jinhui ZHOU received her BSc degree in Water Conservancy and Hydropower Engineering in 2014 and her MSc degree in Hydrology and Water Resources in 2016 at the Sun Yat-sen University. During MSc Jinhui published 2 SCI papers related to urban flood risk warning model and assessing the long-term impact of urbanization on run-off using a remote-sensing-supported hydrological model respectively, and finished graduation thesis on the topic of Analysis of Extreme Rainfall and Flood Response under Climate Change in Liujiang River Basin. Over the past 3 years, Jinhui worked as an environmental engineer and researcher in China. Her job is mainly about developing and applying hydrology and water quality models to explore local environmental and ecological issues in 3 river/lake basins and an urban area, with the aim of providing plan to mitigate the environmental impact on local watersheds. Jinhui’s research is focused on assessing the environmental impacts of future nitrogen dispersal across global watersheds. Due to extensive farming method, the large amount of nutrients losses after fertilization have a great impact on local watersheds and coastal zones. The aim of Jinhui’s project is to evaluate the influence of nitrogen losses on global water quality under different shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) up to the year 2050 by using nutrient model IMAGE-GNM.

name: Droovi De Zilva
summary: Droovi started as a PhD candidate at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in May 2023. He is working for the (Circular Collaboration) CirCol NWO Project. His research involves using Industrial Ecology concepts to expand Value creation within the circular and emission free housing transition in the Netherlands. Droovi has a Bachelor’s degree in Global Sustainability Science, with a specialisation in Energy & Resources, from Utrecht University. He graduated from the Master Energy Science from Utrecht University in October 2022. During his Master consultancy project, he contributed to assessing the environmental impact of packaging of the Dutch Colon Cancer Screening programme (Bevolkingsonderzoek Darmkanker). During his Master internship, he consulted the start-up Caffe Inc on the environmental footprint of their spent coffee ground processing system and advised them on how to reduce their CO2 and Energy footprint. For his Master Thesis, he investigated the potential of a decentralised pyrolysis-based plastic waste management system for managing campus plastic waste at the Utrecht Science Park, primarily using MFA, LCA and energy analysis methods. Droovi is part of Work Package 4 of the CirCol project which is titled “Accrual of broader values”. He will be using namely Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment and Material Flow Analysis, to investigate the mismatch between financial value and the broader socioeconomic and environmental benefits of different circular and emission free renovation options. Using these methods to transparently show the long-term benefits of considering environmental and socioeconomic value will enable relevant actors to develop more circular practices and enable better collaboration between actors in the construction industry.

name: Kimber Zonneveld
summary: Evolutionary biologist focused on plant-microbe symbiosis to support sustainable ecosystems. Kimber Zonneveld is a biologist focusing on the interactions between soil, plants, and microbes. Kimber has a background in Life Sciences (BSc, Amsterdam University College) and Evolutionary Biology (MSc, Leiden University). During the MSc internships, Kimber researched the complex interactions between cycads and their symbiotic microbiomes, which reside in specialized organs called coralloid roots. Through this work, Kimber gained experience in NGS techniques, biogeographical modelling, and population genetics, while collaborating with non-scientific stakeholders across the Netherlands and Mexico. The foundational research on co-symbiotic microbiomes now serves as the basis for Kimber’s current PhD project, which focuses on soil and microbiome health to support protein crop growth. Kimber Zonneveld works as a PhD candidate in the REAP2SOW project, which focuses on integrating protein crops into Dutch agriculture to support the protein transition.

name: Aysegül Çelik
summary: Aysegul started as a PhD candidate at the Industrial Ecology department of CML in September 2025. Her research focuses on Actor-level Food System Footprinting for a sustainable food transition.
